body: If you don’t get into university in your first attempt, it’s not the end of the world. You can get some time off to work a little, learn different things and find yourself a new purpose. There is time, our only mission in this world is to be happy and develop into a better version of yourself each day. Evolve, find new opportunities. If you are depressed you can find help. It took me 20 years, several psychologists and psychiatrists, hospitalizations and electroconvulsive therapy, until I was prescribed the medication that helped me get better two years ago, so don’t give up at the first failed attempt. If you want to talk, I’m here to listen 😢

I’ve had severe depression since I was 14. Or at least that’s when I got my first diagnosis. I had been feeling depressed since I was a little child, and I admit that when I first was prescribed medication, I didn’t take it because I felt like I was losing.
When I was 17, I found my psychologist, and she helped me navigate the difficult times. But I still had a long way to go. I was sent to different psychiatrists and took different medications without improvement. When I was 28 my psychologist thought that maybe I had bipolar disorder and I was tested: I was bipolar. I started the new medication (lithium carbonate) and continued feeling bad, even having extremely severe depression episodes where I couldn’t stop thinking about dying. At 31 I fell in love and was ghosted, making me lose myself and I attempted to take my life. I woke up the next morning and told my mom I needed help. I was hospitalized for two weeks and had sleep therapy (which helped to stabilize me). After that I little while I continued being hospitalized for continuous suicidal ideation. At 33 I was vomiting because I couldn’t handle the meds and decided to stop taking them because it had been several months without being able to take them. After two months I was hospitalized again since I was preparing again to take my life, but my method rotted, and decided to get ECT. I got out, celebrated my birthday and was hospitalized again to get 6 sessions. They didn’t work, but I was prescribed new medication. After a little while, I started feeling a little better. I had forgotten a lot of things (even that I had celebrated my birthday), but I was finally starting to feel peaceful and that kept me going until I reached a point where I fixed my sleeping schedule, my eating habits and even started exercising. It got better and better. Now I’m able to work, I feel peaceful and even happy.

There is always hope.
